body.x: GeoWind (CEO Young June Jeon) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), and conducted an interview at the AVING Media Stage inside the Seoul Pavilion during the exhibition period.

GeoWind is a startup that researches and develops sustainable energy solutions based on urban wind power technology. The company is pursuing commercialization by proposing a new concept of wind power systems that combine spatial and operational efficiency, enabling local renewable energy self-sufficiency with designs that harmonize with urban aesthetics and atmosphere.

Going forward, GeoWind plans to expand its proprietary eco-friendly energy model into education, public, and everyday infrastructure, while further advancing its technology into an integrated platform that combines renewable energy with data and infrastructure.

At CES 2026, GeoWind showcased its core technology and product, the urban vertical-axis wind turbine “GW1200.” Unlike conventional horizontal-axis turbines, GW1200 applies an icosahedron-based geodesic structure, enabling stable rotation and power generation even in turbulent environments with low wind speeds or frequently changing wind directions.

The system also allows installation in limited spaces and features a modular structure that flexibly scales size and capacity. In addition, the design minimizes noise and vibration during operation, while its high torque-to-size ratio supports use across diverse environments, including urban buildings and rooftops, coastal areas, and off-grid regions.

Scalability is another key strength of GW1200. Each turbine can integrate various sensors, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed sensors, allowing it to serve not only regional power self-sufficiency needs but also as a climate and environmental data measurement system for smart cities.

Based on these multifaceted strengths, GeoWind received a CES 2026 Innovation Award in the Sustainability & Energy Transition category. With this international recognition, the company plans to accelerate the expansion of its “climate intelligence infrastructure” strategy and move forward with global market entry.

Young June Jeon, CEO of GeoWind, said, “GW1200 has the potential to establish itself not merely as a power generation device, but as a new type of infrastructure required by cities and local communities.” He added, “Our next goal is to expand wind turbines into regional climate data hubs, and the CES Innovation Award will serve as an important milestone that accelerates this journey.”

Jeon continued, “Through our participation in CES, we plan to expand global partnerships and collaborate with a wide range of industries to introduce new business models that combine renewable energy with data infrastructure,” adding, “We aim to grow into a platform company that goes beyond sustainable energy solutions to support climate response and ESG management.”

body.x: The company participated in CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026 supported a total of 70 startups with participation from 19 startup support organizations based in Seoul, including the Seoul Business Agency, district offices, related institutions, and universities. The 70 exhibiting companies were composed of startups offering products and services based on advanced technologies such as AI, mobility, and healthcare. Among them, selected outstanding companies were given the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled.
